**Sean Parker** (born December 3, 1979) is an American entrepreneur and philanthropist, most notable for co-founding the file-sharing computer service Napster, and was the first president of the social networking website Facebook. He also co-founded Plaxo, Causes, Airtime.com, and Brigade, an online platform for civic engagement.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-reutersnapster-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-WSJ_041609-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-7) He is the founder and chairman of the Parker Foundation, which focuses on life sciences, global public health, and civic engagement.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-8) According to _Forbes_, as of May 2025, Parker's estimated net worth stood at US$3.0 billion, placing him in the top 1,250 richest individuals in the world.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-Forbes-9)
texts.1: Parker was born in Herndon, Virginia, to Diane Parker, a TV advertising broker, and Bruce Parker, a U.S. government oceanographer and chief scientist at NOAA.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-venturebeat-10) When Parker was seven, his father taught him how to program on an Atari 800.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2) Parker's father, who put his family before his entrepreneurial dreams, told Parker, "if you are going to take risks, take them early before you have a family."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-slate-11) In his teens, Parker's hobbies were hacking and programming.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) One night, while hacking into the network of a _Fortune_ 500 company, Parker was unable to log out after his father confiscated his computer keyboard.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Because his IP address was exposed, FBI agents tracked down the 16-year-old.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Since Parker was under 18, he was sentenced to community service.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)
texts.2: Parker attended Oakton High School in Fairfax County, Virginia for two years before transferring to Chantilly High School in 1996 for his junior and senior years.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-connectionnews-12) While there, Parker wrote a letter to the school administration and persuaded them to count the time he spent coding in the computer lab as a foreign language class.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-connectionnews-12) Consequently, towards the end of Parker's senior year at Chantilly, he was mostly writing code and starting companies.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-connectionnews-12) He graduated in 1998. While still in high school, he interned for Mark Pincus (who would later become the CEO of Zynga) at Pincus's Washington, DC startup FreeLoader.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-13) He won the Virginia state computer science fair for developing a web crawler, and was recruited by the CIA.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2) By his senior year of high school, Parker was earning more than $80,000 a year through various projects, enough to convince his parents to allow him to skip college and pursue a career as an entrepreneur.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)
texts.3: In his childhood, Parker was an avid reader, which was the beginning of his lifelong autodidacticism.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-dealbook-14) Several media profiles refer to Parker as a genius.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-19) He considers his time at Napster to be his college education, calling it "Napster University", since he became well-versed in intellectual property law, corporate finance, and entrepreneurship.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-20)
texts.4: When Parker was 15, he met 14-year-old Shawn Fanning over the Internet, where the pair bonded over topics such as programming, theoretical physics, and hacking.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-21) A few years later, Parker and Fanning, a student at Northeastern University, cofounded Napster, a free file-sharing service for music.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-reutersnapster-5) Parker raised the initial $50,000, and they launched Napster in June 1999.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-businessinsiderairtime-22) Within a year, the service had tens of millions of users.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Napster was opposed by recording labels, the Recording Industry Association of America, and the heavy metal band Metallica,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-venturebeat-10) among others. [Lawsuits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica_v._Napster,_Inc. "Metallica v.
texts.5:
Napster, Inc.") by various industry associations eventually shut down the service.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-BBC_270700-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-BBC_260302-24) Napster has been called the fastest-growing business of all time, is credited with revolutionizing the music industry, and is considered by some to be a precursor to iTunes.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-29)
In November 2002, Parker launched Plaxo, an online address book and social networking service that integrated with Microsoft Outlook.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-WIRED_111202-30) Plaxo was an early social networking tool, which later influenced the growth of companies LinkedIn, Zynga, and Facebook.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruptionplaxo-31) Plaxo was one of the first products to build virality into its launch, and that earned it 20 million users.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-33) Two years after founding Plaxo, Parker was ousted by the company's financiers, Sequoia Capital and Ram Shriram, in an acrimonious exit that reportedly involved the investors hiring private investigators to follow him.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-35)
texts.6: In 2004, Parker saw a site called "The Facebook" on the computer of his roommate's girlfriend, who was a student at Stanford.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Parker had experience in the social networking industry as an early advisor to Friendster and its founder, Jonathan Abrams, for which he was given a small amount of stock in 2003.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-facebookeffect-36) Parker met with Mark Zuckerberg and Eduardo Saverin, and a few months later joined the five-month-old company as its president.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-facebookeffect-36) According to Peter Thiel, Parker was the first to see potential in the company to be "really big", and that "if Mark ever had any second thoughts, Sean was the one who cut that off".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)
texts.7:
As president, Parker brought on Thiel as Facebook's first investor.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) In the initial round of funding, he negotiated for Zuckerberg to retain three of Facebook's five board seats, which gave Zuckerberg control of the company and allowed Facebook the freedom to remain a private company.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Additionally, Parker is said to have championed Facebook's clean user interface and developed its photo-sharing function.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-web2summit-38) Zuckerberg notes that "Sean was pivotal in helping Facebook transform from a college project into a real company."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-consume-39)
During a party in 2005, police entered and searched a vacation home Parker was renting and found cocaine.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Parker was arrested on suspicion of drug possession but was not charged.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) This event caused Facebook investors to pressure Parker into resigning as president.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-40) However, after stepping down, Parker continued to remain involved with Facebook's growth, and met regularly with Zuckerberg.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-41) The event was later dramatized in the movie _The Social Network_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-abcnews-42)
texts.8:
In 2017, during an interview with Axios, Parker expressed concerns about the role of Facebook in society, saying that it "exploit[s] a vulnerability in human psychology" as it creates a "social-validation feedback loop". Parker stated that he was "something of a conscientious objector" to using social media.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-43)
In 2006, Parker became a managing partner at Founders Fund, a San Francisco-based venture-capital fund founded by Peter Thiel.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-44) Founders Fund is focused on investing in early-stage companies, has $500 million in aggregate capital, and has invested in Quantcast, Path, and Knewton.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-45) Parker was given carte blanche by Thiel when finding investments.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-46) In 2014, Parker stepped down from his role at Founders Fund to focus on other projects.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-47) Parker has also hosted The TechFellow Awards, a partnership between TechCrunch and Founders Fund that annually gives 20 entrepreneurs $100,000 each to invest in startups.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-49)
texts.12:
In 2007, Parker founded Causes, originally one of the earliest Facebook applications, as a philanthropic service that uses social media to connect charities with their supporters and potential donors and then communicates that connection to the user's network of friends.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-68) By 2013, 186 million people had joined Causes, donating over $50 million to 60,000 non-profits.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-70)
In June 2015, Parker announced[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-71) a $600 million contribution to launch the Parker Foundation, which focuses on three areas - life sciences, global public health, and civic engagement.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-73) It takes an interdisciplinary approach to large-scale challenges, combining insight, capital, science and technology, organization building, and public policy.
texts.13:
### Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy
[edit]
Parker donated $250 million to create the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy, in April 2016. The funds initially went to over 300 scientists at 40 laboratories, in six institutions.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-74)
Starting in 2016, the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy scientists funded a clinical trial to test the next wave of cancer-fighting T-cells engineered using the CRISPR gene-editing technology.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-fortune8-75) The trial was the first in the United States to test CRISPR-modified cells in humans.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-MIT3-76) The trial is led by the University of Pennsylvania and is also conducted at University of California, San Francisco and the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-MIT3-76)
In November 2017, _Science_ published a study from Parker Institute researchers at MD Anderson Cancer Center showing that melanoma patients who have specific types of bacteria and greater microbial diversity in their gut microbiome responded better to an anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor versus those with less diversity.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-gut-77) Based on this work, the Parker Institute is collaborating with MD Anderson and industry partner Seres Therapeutics to launch a microbiome-cancer immunotherapy clinical trial for advanced melanoma patients.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-gut-77)
Parker is on the boards of these nonprofits:
texts.14:
### Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy
*   Obama Foundation[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-78)  
*   Global Citizen[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-79)  
*   Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-80)  
*   Parker Foundation[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-81)  
*   Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-82)
In February 2015, Parker was ranked number five on the _Chronicle of Philanthropy's_ 2014 Philanthropy 50 list.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-83) In August 2018, Parker was nominated as a _Wired_ "Icon" along with Alex Marson for his research in DNA programming and genome editing in the fight against cancer.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-84) He's also been named one of _Town and Country'_ s Top 50 Philanthropists and was named in_Time_'s Healthcare 50 for his work in connecting cancer research.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-86) In 2016, he was given the Pontifical Key Philanthropy Award by Cardinal Gianfranco Ravasi at the Vatican for his cancer work.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-87)
texts.15:
## Political donations and activism
[edit]
Parker has made substantial donations to both sides of U.S. party politics; his allegedly "nonpartisan" approach favors contributions to "elected officials who have shown themselves willing to work across the aisle".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-88) He favored Democrats and progressive causes such as campaign finance reform[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-89) and gun control;[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-90) he has spoken out in favor of higher taxes, particularly for the "wealthy and super wealthy", and in favor of higher capital-gains taxes.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-sfbg-67) Parker has also supported middle-of-the-road Republican candidates and super PACs, favoring "economically moderate" conservatives and candidates with a demonstrated interest in compromise and deal-making.
texts.16:
## Political donations and activism
In Washington, DC, he has met with Republican lawmakers about ways of encouraging economic investment in struggling areas of the country.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-92) He has also supported cannabis law reform[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-93) and in 2010, following the example of donations by Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz (totaling $70,000) donated $100,000 to the 2010 California Proposition 19 campaign to legalize marijuana in that state[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-guardian-2010-10-10-94) and $400,000 to the Democratic Party backed 2016 California Proposition 63 campaign to require background checks for all ammunition purchases.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-95) Parker will donate $250 million to launch a new institute aimed at developing more effective cancer treatments by fostering collaboration among leading researchers in the field.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-96) For the 2016 presidential election, Parker created a social ballot guide for voters to help each other pledge to vote.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-97)

**Sean Parker** (born December 3, 1979) is an American entrepreneur and philanthropist, most notable for co-founding the file-sharing computer service Napster, and was the first president of the social networking website Facebook. He also co-founded Plaxo, Causes, Airtime.com, and Brigade, an online platform for civic engagement.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-reutersnapster-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-WSJ_041609-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-7) He is the founder and chairman of the Parker Foundation, which focuses on life sciences, global public health, and civic engagement.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-8) According to _Forbes_, as of May 2025, Parker's estimated net worth stood at US$3.0 billion, placing him in the top 1,250 richest individuals in the world.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-Forbes-9)

Parker was born in Herndon, Virginia, to Diane Parker, a TV advertising broker, and Bruce Parker, a U.S. government oceanographer and chief scientist at NOAA.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-venturebeat-10) When Parker was seven, his father taught him how to program on an Atari 800.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2) Parker's father, who put his family before his entrepreneurial dreams, told Parker, "if you are going to take risks, take them early before you have a family."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-slate-11) In his teens, Parker's hobbies were hacking and programming.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) One night, while hacking into the network of a _Fortune_ 500 company, Parker was unable to log out after his father confiscated his computer keyboard.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Because his IP address was exposed, FBI agents tracked down the 16-year-old.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Since Parker was under 18, he was sentenced to community service.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)

Parker attended Oakton High School in Fairfax County, Virginia for two years before transferring to Chantilly High School in 1996 for his junior and senior years.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-connectionnews-12) While there, Parker wrote a letter to the school administration and persuaded them to count the time he spent coding in the computer lab as a foreign language class.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-connectionnews-12) Consequently, towards the end of Parker's senior year at Chantilly, he was mostly writing code and starting companies.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-connectionnews-12) He graduated in 1998. While still in high school, he interned for Mark Pincus (who would later become the CEO of Zynga) at Pincus's Washington, DC startup FreeLoader.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-13) He won the Virginia state computer science fair for developing a web crawler, and was recruited by the CIA.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2) By his senior year of high school, Parker was earning more than $80,000 a year through various projects, enough to convince his parents to allow him to skip college and pursue a career as an entrepreneur.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)

In his childhood, Parker was an avid reader, which was the beginning of his lifelong autodidacticism.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-dealbook-14) Several media profiles refer to Parker as a genius.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-19) He considers his time at Napster to be his college education, calling it "Napster University", since he became well-versed in intellectual property law, corporate finance, and entrepreneurship.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-20)

When Parker was 15, he met 14-year-old Shawn Fanning over the Internet, where the pair bonded over topics such as programming, theoretical physics, and hacking.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-21) A few years later, Parker and Fanning, a student at Northeastern University, cofounded Napster, a free file-sharing service for music.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-reutersnapster-5) Parker raised the initial $50,000, and they launched Napster in June 1999.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-businessinsiderairtime-22) Within a year, the service had tens of millions of users.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Napster was opposed by recording labels, the Recording Industry Association of America, and the heavy metal band Metallica,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-venturebeat-10) among others. [Lawsuits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica_v._Napster,_Inc. "Metallica v.

Napster, Inc.") by various industry associations eventually shut down the service.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-BBC_270700-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-BBC_260302-24) Napster has been called the fastest-growing business of all time, is credited with revolutionizing the music industry, and is considered by some to be a precursor to iTunes.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-29)
In November 2002, Parker launched Plaxo, an online address book and social networking service that integrated with Microsoft Outlook.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-WIRED_111202-30) Plaxo was an early social networking tool, which later influenced the growth of companies LinkedIn, Zynga, and Facebook.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruptionplaxo-31) Plaxo was one of the first products to build virality into its launch, and that earned it 20 million users.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-33) Two years after founding Plaxo, Parker was ousted by the company's financiers, Sequoia Capital and Ram Shriram, in an acrimonious exit that reportedly involved the investors hiring private investigators to follow him.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-35)

In 2004, Parker saw a site called "The Facebook" on the computer of his roommate's girlfriend, who was a student at Stanford.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Parker had experience in the social networking industry as an early advisor to Friendster and its founder, Jonathan Abrams, for which he was given a small amount of stock in 2003.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-facebookeffect-36) Parker met with Mark Zuckerberg and Eduardo Saverin, and a few months later joined the five-month-old company as its president.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-facebookeffect-36) According to Peter Thiel, Parker was the first to see potential in the company to be "really big", and that "if Mark ever had any second thoughts, Sean was the one who cut that off".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3)

As president, Parker brought on Thiel as Facebook's first investor.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) In the initial round of funding, he negotiated for Zuckerberg to retain three of Facebook's five board seats, which gave Zuckerberg control of the company and allowed Facebook the freedom to remain a private company.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Additionally, Parker is said to have championed Facebook's clean user interface and developed its photo-sharing function.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-web2summit-38) Zuckerberg notes that "Sean was pivotal in helping Facebook transform from a college project into a real company."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-forbesdisruption-2)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-consume-39)
During a party in 2005, police entered and searched a vacation home Parker was renting and found cocaine.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) Parker was arrested on suspicion of drug possession but was not charged.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-vanityfair-3) This event caused Facebook investors to pressure Parker into resigning as president.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-40) However, after stepping down, Parker continued to remain involved with Facebook's growth, and met regularly with Zuckerberg.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-41) The event was later dramatized in the movie _The Social Network_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-abcnews-42)

In 2017, during an interview with Axios, Parker expressed concerns about the role of Facebook in society, saying that it "exploit[s] a vulnerability in human psychology" as it creates a "social-validation feedback loop". Parker stated that he was "something of a conscientious objector" to using social media.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-43)
In 2006, Parker became a managing partner at Founders Fund, a San Francisco-based venture-capital fund founded by Peter Thiel.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-44) Founders Fund is focused on investing in early-stage companies, has $500 million in aggregate capital, and has invested in Quantcast, Path, and Knewton.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-45) Parker was given carte blanche by Thiel when finding investments.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-46) In 2014, Parker stepped down from his role at Founders Fund to focus on other projects.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-47) Parker has also hosted The TechFellow Awards, a partnership between TechCrunch and Founders Fund that annually gives 20 entrepreneurs $100,000 each to invest in startups.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-49)

In 2007, Parker founded Causes, originally one of the earliest Facebook applications, as a philanthropic service that uses social media to connect charities with their supporters and potential donors and then communicates that connection to the user's network of friends.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-68) By 2013, 186 million people had joined Causes, donating over $50 million to 60,000 non-profits.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-70)
In June 2015, Parker announced[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-71) a $600 million contribution to launch the Parker Foundation, which focuses on three areas - life sciences, global public health, and civic engagement.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-73) It takes an interdisciplinary approach to large-scale challenges, combining insight, capital, science and technology, organization building, and public policy.

### Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy
[edit]
Parker donated $250 million to create the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy, in April 2016. The funds initially went to over 300 scientists at 40 laboratories, in six institutions.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-74)
Starting in 2016, the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy scientists funded a clinical trial to test the next wave of cancer-fighting T-cells engineered using the CRISPR gene-editing technology.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-fortune8-75) The trial was the first in the United States to test CRISPR-modified cells in humans.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-MIT3-76) The trial is led by the University of Pennsylvania and is also conducted at University of California, San Francisco and the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-MIT3-76)
In November 2017, _Science_ published a study from Parker Institute researchers at MD Anderson Cancer Center showing that melanoma patients who have specific types of bacteria and greater microbial diversity in their gut microbiome responded better to an anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor versus those with less diversity.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-gut-77) Based on this work, the Parker Institute is collaborating with MD Anderson and industry partner Seres Therapeutics to launch a microbiome-cancer immunotherapy clinical trial for advanced melanoma patients.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-gut-77)
Parker is on the boards of these nonprofits:

### Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy
*   Obama Foundation[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-78)  
*   Global Citizen[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-79)  
*   Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-80)  
*   Parker Foundation[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-81)  
*   Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-82)
In February 2015, Parker was ranked number five on the _Chronicle of Philanthropy's_ 2014 Philanthropy 50 list.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-83) In August 2018, Parker was nominated as a _Wired_ "Icon" along with Alex Marson for his research in DNA programming and genome editing in the fight against cancer.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-84) He's also been named one of _Town and Country'_ s Top 50 Philanthropists and was named in_Time_'s Healthcare 50 for his work in connecting cancer research.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-86) In 2016, he was given the Pontifical Key Philanthropy Award by Cardinal Gianfranco Ravasi at the Vatican for his cancer work.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-87)

## Political donations and activism
[edit]
Parker has made substantial donations to both sides of U.S. party politics; his allegedly "nonpartisan" approach favors contributions to "elected officials who have shown themselves willing to work across the aisle".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-88) He favored Democrats and progressive causes such as campaign finance reform[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-89) and gun control;[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-90) he has spoken out in favor of higher taxes, particularly for the "wealthy and super wealthy", and in favor of higher capital-gains taxes.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-sfbg-67) Parker has also supported middle-of-the-road Republican candidates and super PACs, favoring "economically moderate" conservatives and candidates with a demonstrated interest in compromise and deal-making.

## Political donations and activism
In Washington, DC, he has met with Republican lawmakers about ways of encouraging economic investment in struggling areas of the country.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-92) He has also supported cannabis law reform[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-93) and in 2010, following the example of donations by Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz (totaling $70,000) donated $100,000 to the 2010 California Proposition 19 campaign to legalize marijuana in that state[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-guardian-2010-10-10-94) and $400,000 to the Democratic Party backed 2016 California Proposition 63 campaign to require background checks for all ammunition purchases.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-95) Parker will donate $250 million to launch a new institute aimed at developing more effective cancer treatments by fostering collaboration among leading researchers in the field.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-96) For the 2016 presidential election, Parker created a social ballot guide for voters to help each other pledge to vote.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker#cite_note-97)

Source: https://www.sportspro.com/news/sponsorship-marketing/afa-argentine-football-association-socios-sponsorship-payments-president-january-2026/
Title: AFA partnership with Socios in doubt due to payment concerns
Chunks: 0,1
*   **Socios stops payments to intermediaries after less than US$500k of US$9m reached AFA**  
*   **Company calls for resignation of AFA president Claudio Tapia**  
*   **Socios CEO Alexandre Dreyfus calls on other AFA sponsors to follow suit**
* * *
**The Argentine Football Association’s (AFA) partnership with Socios is in jeopardy after the blockchain-based fan engagement platform halted its support and called for the resignation of the organisation’s president.**
Chiliz-owned Socios has been a major sponsor of the AFA since 2021 but the company has now stopped payments to intermediaries associated with the national soccer governing body and demanded a full audit.
Socios and Chiliz chief executive Alexandre Dreyfus said on LinkedIn that the company has “transferred over US$9 million intended for Argentine football” since 2021 but cited reports indicating that significantly less had actually reached the AFA directly.
“We refuse to continue funding offshore entities that have provided zero services to us,” added Dreyfus. “We have demanded a full audit and requested that future payments go strictly and directly to the AFA.”
In addition to requesting for AFA president Claudio Tapia to resign, Dreyfus called for other AFA sponsors, including Adidas, American Express, Coca-Cola, Fanatics and Lexar, to take the same stance as Socios.
As reported by Argentine newspaper La Nación, of the US$9 million sent by Socios since 2021, less than US$500,000 has arrived directly to the AFA.
The incident is the latest controversy for the AFA under the presidency of Tapia, following accusations of links to money laundering and corruption, which he has distanced himself from.
This isn’t the first time that Socios and the AFA have clashed during their partnership. In 2021, judicial mediation was required after both parties filed complaints against each other for breach of contract. At the time, the AFA had signed a partnership with Binance, which also operates in the blockchain space, that included naming rights to the Primera Division, which were held by Socios.
The dispute was later settled and the pair extended their deal through 2026.

Socios is a prolific sponsor in sport and has partnerships with more than 100 teams across the likes of the Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Ligue 1, the National Football League (NFL), the National Basketball Association (NBA) and Formula One.

Title: Major AFA sponsor withdraws payments and requests Tapia’s resignation
Chunks: 0,1,2
Argentine Football Association (AFA) sponsor _Socios.com_ announced on Tuesday it’ll be withdrawing its support for the governing body until president Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia resigns.
The company, one of the AFA’s biggest sponsors since 2020, decided to halt money transfers to AFA intermediaries and requested an audit of Argentine football’s governing body.
The news, originally reported by Argentine outlet _La Nación_, was later confirmed by company CEO Alexandre Dreyfus through his _X_ account.
“Transparency in football is non-negotiable,” Dreyfus wrote. “Today, _Socios.com_ has officially halted payments to ‘intermediaries’ associated with the [AFA] and requested the resignation of [Tapia].”
Dreyfus added that, since 2021, the company has transferred over US$9 million, and found it ‘disgusting’ that reports suggest now only US$500,000 actually reached AFA’s coffers.
“We refuse to continue funding offshore entities that have provided zero services to us,” he said. “We have demanded a full audit and requested that future payments go strictly and directly to the AFA.”
Dreyfus called on other AFA sponsors such as Adidas, American Express and Coca-Cola to join them, saying “collective action” is required in the interest of “the integrity of the football industry.”

## Socios.com
Socios.com is a blockchain-based platform that allows fans to purchase “Fan Tokens” which lets them influence minor club decisions through voting, access promotions, and participate in games, using cryptocurrency Chiliz.
The company also works with some of the biggest names in football such as European giants FC Barcelona, PSG and Manchester City, as well as South American powerhouses like Flamengo, River Plate and Independiente, and teams from other sports.
It’s not the first time _Socios.com_ and the AFA have clashed.
In 2021, a judicial mediation was required as both parties filed complaints against each other due to breach of contract, with the company requesting information on who the beneficiaries of the payments were. However, the deal was extended through to 2026 in 2022.

## Tapia ‘not worried’ about corruption scandal
As controversies mount around him, Tapia distanced himself from the scandals, saying he’s “not worried” about the barrage of accusations linking him to money laundering, corruption and other crimes.
The AFA president has been in the spotlight since the end of last year, as Argentine football’s governing body has been linked to money laundering claims involving financial firm Sur Finanzas and corruption allegations, which got Tapia reported to South American football confederation CONMEBOL’s ethics committee.
“It’s two different realities, the one in the media and the one you see around people,” he told _La Nacion_ on Tuesday. “I don’t pay attention to the other stuff, it’s all just in the media.”
The AFA boss assured he’s “not worried” since so far he hasn’t been formally charged.
Tapia is on vacation at quintessential Argentine beach town Mar del Plata, where he insists fans give him continuous shows of affection, something he admitted to enjoy.
“My legs hurt from sitting down and standing up for the photos, my knees are wrecked,” he joked. “Everywhere I go it’s like this. This is real life.”
Tapia said he used to be worried about his family being affected by the news, but hasn’t since his children became adults.
The AFA boss is father to three sons and a daughter. The eldest, Matías, was a professional footballer and is now the president of Barracas Central, the club his father presided over for nearly 20 years, while the second-born, Iván, is also a professional player.

# Celtics Announce Official Partnership with Socios.com
Boston Celtics
July 7, 2021 10:07 AM EDT
addByline("Boston Celtics","Celtics.com","Celtics");
**BOSTON** - The Boston Celtics today announced their official partnership with Socios.com, allowing the 17-time World Champions to join forces with the leading blockchain provider for the global sports and entertainment industry.
Socios.com will have a digital presence on Celtics.com and serve as the presenting partner of the team’s website, placing it at the forefront of the Celtics’ primary hub for relevant news, updates, video highlights, and information pertaining to the franchise. They will also have the ability to leverage the Celtics marks and logos in connection with various Socios.com international marketing activities.
“A large part of the Celtics brand is made up of the great fans that support the organization across local, national, and global levels, and we’re excited to find a partner that values fan engagement as much as we do,” said Senior Vice President of Corporate Partnerships & Business Development Ted Dalton. “We’re always looking for innovative ways to reach Celtics fans and look forward to our partnership with Socios.com.”
“The Boston Celtics are an iconic, world-renowned brand and I’m delighted they have become the latest major US-based sporting organization to join our rapidly expanding network,” said Socios.com CEO Alexandre Dreyfus. “Socios.com is fast developing into a global fan engagement powerhouse, where passive fans are being transitioned into active participants. This is the start of an exciting partnership that we believe can eventually lead to greatly enhanced fan engagement for fans of the Celtics around the world.”

# Celtics Announce Official Partnership with Socios.com
### Partnership reflects Socios.com’s expansion efforts throughout international, United States sports industries
The Celtics now join Socios.com’s 40+ roster that includes major sporting organizations across soccer, F1, MMA, esports, and cricket. The partnership also represents Socios.com’s growing expansion into the US sports industry, with the Celtics becoming the latest NBA franchise to partner with Socios.com.

# Socios halts payments to AFA over fee transparency concerns
The blockchain platform has claimed that only a fraction of its fees have reached the governing body.
Susan LingeswaranJanuary 13, 2026
Share
*   Copy Link  
*   Share on X  
*   Share on Linkedin  
*   Share on Facebook
The company has called on the AFA’s other commercial partners to join them in halting payments until the situation is resolved. (Socios)
Socios, the blockchain-based fan engagement platform, has stopped its sponsorship payments to “intermediaries” associated with the Argentine Football Association (AFA) after allegations that only a fraction of its fees have reached the governing body.
Announcing the move on networking platform LinkedIn, Alexandre Dreyfus, the chief executive and founder of Socios’ parent company, The Chilliz Group, called on the AFA’s fellow commercial partners, adidas, American Express, Lexar, Fanatic, The Coca-Cola Company, and others to follow suit.

Drefus said since 2021, it has sent $9 million in sponsorship fees to intermediary companies as part of its agreement as the AFA’s official fan token platform until at least this year, but only a fraction – around $480,000 – had reached the AFA.
He added:“While we do not have possession of their internal bank records to verify this exact figure, if true, it is absolutely disgusting.
“We refuse to continue funding offshore entities that have provided zero services to us. We have demanded a full audit and requested that future payments go strictly and directly to the AFA.
“We must take collective action to ensure funds go where they belong: to the sport and the institution. We must do this in the interest of the fans, the Selección, and the integrity of the football industry.”
In a statement, Socios said they will no longer send funds through the AFA’s intermediaries, with any future payments “made in a way that guarantees the funds are transferred directly to the AFA as the legitimate rights holder, without intermediaries.
“We are particularly concerned about the use of third-party or offshore entities —including Q22 Services Limited (Guernsey), Stratega Consulting USA LLC (Delaware), Odeoma Gestión SL (Spain), and Tourprodenter LLC (Florida).
“None of these entities ever provided services to Socios.com, nor did they present, negotiate, or manage our sponsorship agreements with the AFA.”
The company lso called for the resignation or suspension of AFA president Claudio Tapia, AFA treasurer Pablo Toviggino, and other senior officials.
Originally from France and headquartered in Malta, Socios has partnered with a range of top sports properties. Along with the AFA, it has had partnerships with soccer’s Barcelona, PSG, Manchester City, Juventus, and Flamengo, as well as clubs in basketball’s NBA, American football’s NFL, and motor racing’s Formula 1.

*   **Socios stops payments to intermediaries after less than US$500k of US$9m reached AFA**  
*   **Company calls for resignation of AFA president Claudio Tapia**  
*   **Socios CEO Alexandre Dreyfus calls on other AFA sponsors to follow suit**
* * *
**The Argentine Football Association’s (AFA) partnership with Socios is in jeopardy after the blockchain-based fan engagement platform halted its support and called for the resignation of the organisation’s president.**
Chiliz-owned Socios has been a major sponsor of the AFA since 2021 but the company has now stopped payments to intermediaries associated with the national soccer governing body and demanded a full audit.
Socios and Chiliz chief executive Alexandre Dreyfus said on LinkedIn that the company has “transferred over US$9 million intended for Argentine football” since 2021 but cited reports indicating that significantly less had actually reached the AFA directly.
“We refuse to continue funding offshore entities that have provided zero services to us,” added Dreyfus. “We have demanded a full audit and requested that future payments go strictly and directly to the AFA.”
In addition to requesting for AFA president Claudio Tapia to resign, Dreyfus called for other AFA sponsors, including Adidas, American Express, Coca-Cola, Fanatics and Lexar, to take the same stance as Socios.
As reported by Argentine newspaper La Nación, of the US$9 million sent by Socios since 2021, less than US$500,000 has arrived directly to the AFA.
The incident is the latest controversy for the AFA under the presidency of Tapia, following accusations of links to money laundering and corruption, which he has distanced himself from.
This isn’t the first time that Socios and the AFA have clashed during their partnership. In 2021, judicial mediation was required after both parties filed complaints against each other for breach of contract. At the time, the AFA had signed a partnership with Binance, which also operates in the blockchain space, that included naming rights to the Primera Division, which were held by Socios.
The dispute was later settled and the pair extended their deal through 2026.

Susan LingeswaranJanuary 13, 2026

Socios, the blockchain-based fan engagement platform, has stopped its sponsorship payments to “intermediaries” associated with the Argentine Football Association (AFA) after allegations that only a fraction of its fees have reached the governing body.
Announcing the move on networking platform LinkedIn, Alexandre Dreyfus, the chief executive and founder of Socios’ parent company, The Chilliz Group, called on the AFA’s fellow commercial partners, adidas, American Express, Lexar, Fanatic, The Coca-Cola Company, and others to follow suit.

Drefus said since 2021, it has sent $9 million in sponsorship fees to intermediary companies as part of its agreement as the AFA’s official fan token platform until at least this year, but only a fraction – around $480,000 – had reached the AFA.
He added:“While we do not have possession of their internal bank records to verify this exact figure, if true, it is absolutely disgusting.

In a statement, Socios said they will no longer send funds through the AFA’s intermediaries, with any future payments “made in a way that guarantees the funds are transferred directly to the AFA as the legitimate rights holder, without intermediaries.
“We are particularly concerned about the use of third-party or offshore entities —including Q22 Services Limited (Guernsey), Stratega Consulting USA LLC (Delaware), Odeoma Gestión SL (Spain), and Tourprodenter LLC (Florida).
“None of these entities ever provided services to Socios.com, nor did they present, negotiate, or manage our sponsorship agreements with the AFA.”
The company lso called for the resignation or suspension of AFA president Claudio Tapia, AFA treasurer Pablo Toviggino, and other senior officials.
Originally from France and headquartered in Malta, Socios has partnered with a range of top sports properties. Argentine Football Association (AFA) sponsor _Socios.com_ announced on Tuesday it’ll be withdrawing its support for the governing body until president Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia resigns.
The company, one of the AFA’s biggest sponsors since 2020, decided to halt money transfers to AFA intermediaries and requested an audit of Argentine football’s governing body.
The news, originally reported by Argentine outlet _La Nación_, was later confirmed by company CEO Alexandre Dreyfus through his _X_ account.
“Transparency in football is non-negotiable,” Dreyfus wrote. “Today, _Socios.com_ has officially halted payments to ‘intermediaries’ associated with the [AFA] and requested the resignation of [Tapia].”
Dreyfus added that, since 2021, the company has transferred over US$9 million, and found it ‘disgusting’ that reports suggest now only US$500,000 actually reached AFA’s coffers.
“We refuse to continue funding offshore entities that have provided zero services to us,” he said. “We have demanded a full audit and requested that future payments go strictly and directly to the AFA.”
Dreyfus called on other AFA sponsors such as Adidas, American Express and Coca-Cola to join them, saying “collective action” is required in the interest of “the integrity of the football industry.”
texts.1:
## Socios.com
Socios.com is a blockchain-based platform that allows fans to purchase “Fan Tokens” which lets them influence minor club decisions through voting, access promotions, and participate in games, using cryptocurrency Chiliz.
The company also works with some of the biggest names in football such as European giants FC Barcelona, PSG and Manchester City, as well as South American powerhouses like Flamengo, River Plate and Independiente, and teams from other sports.
It’s not the first time _Socios.com_ and the AFA have clashed.
In 2021, a judicial mediation was required as both parties filed complaints against each other due to breach of contract, with the company requesting information on who the beneficiaries of the payments were. However, the deal was extended through to 2026 in 2022.
texts.2:
## Tapia ‘not worried’ about corruption scandal
As controversies mount around him, Tapia distanced himself from the scandals, saying he’s “not worried” about the barrage of accusations linking him to money laundering, corruption and other crimes.
The AFA president has been in the spotlight since the end of last year, as Argentine football’s governing body has been linked to money laundering claims involving financial firm Sur Finanzas and corruption allegations, which got Tapia reported to South American football confederation CONMEBOL’s ethics committee.
“It’s two different realities, the one in the media and the one you see around people,” he told _La Nacion_ on Tuesday. “I don’t pay attention to the other stuff, it’s all just in the media.”
The AFA boss assured he’s “not worried” since so far he hasn’t been formally charged.
Tapia is on vacation at quintessential Argentine beach town Mar del Plata, where he insists fans give him continuous shows of affection, something he admitted to enjoy.
“My legs hurt from sitting down and standing up for the photos, my knees are wrecked,” he joked. “Everywhere I go it’s like this. This is real life.”
Tapia said he used to be worried about his family being affected by the news, but hasn’t since his children became adults.
The AFA boss is father to three sons and a daughter. The eldest, Matías, was a professional footballer and is now the president of Barracas Central, the club his father presided over for nearly 20 years, while the second-born, Iván, is also a professional player.

### How Many Chiliz (CHZ) Coins Are There in Circulation?
At launch in October 2018, the total supply of CHZ was fixed at 8.8 billion tokens, distributed across early contributors, strategic partners, and exchange sales. Initially, CHZ was issued as an ERC-20 token on Ethereum, with additional compatibility as BEP-2 on Binance Chain and TRC-20 on Tron.
Following the migration to the Chiliz Chain, this fixed-supply model was replaced by a dynamic tokenomics framework designed to ensure the long-term sustainability, security, and growth of the ecosystem. ## About Chiliz
### How Is the Chiliz Network Secured?
The Chiliz Chain is a dedicated Layer-1 blockchain built for the sports and entertainment industries. It is a fork of BNB Smart Chain (BSC), which itself derives from go-Ethereum (geth). This makes the network Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) compatible, allowing it to interact with and execute Ethereum-based smart contracts seamlessly.
Security and consensus on the Chiliz Chain are maintained through a Proof-of-Staked-Authority (PoSA) mechanism — a hybrid model that combines Proof-of-Authority (PoA) and Proof-of-Stake (PoS). Under PoSA, a limited set of validators take turns producing blocks in a PoA fashion, while their ability to serve as validators depends on the amount of CHZ staked in support of them.
Validators are the backbone of the network, responsible for validating transactions, producing blocks, and safeguarding the chain’s integrity. Two types of validators exist:
*   Main Validators – actively produce blocks and commit them to the blockchain.  
*   Candidate Validators – remain in standby and can be promoted if a Main Validator is penalized or becomes unavailable.
Beyond securing the network, validators also play a crucial role in on-chain governance. Their voting power is proportional to the amount of CHZ staked, giving them influence over proposals that shape the evolution of the chain.
Community members can contribute to network security as delegators, by staking their CHZ with validators. Delegators indirectly participate in governance while helping to secure the chain. In return, they receive a share of the rewards earned by validators — sourced from transaction tips and CHZ block rewards.
This staking-driven model ensures that the Chiliz Chain remains secure, efficient, and community-governed, while supporting the creation and management of digital assets tailored to sports and entertainment.

# Chiliz price
## About Chiliz
### How Is the Chiliz Network Secured?
The Chiliz Chain is a dedicated Layer-1 blockchain built for the sports and entertainment industries. It is a fork of BNB Smart Chain (BSC), which itself derives from go-Ethereum (geth). This makes the network Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) compatible, allowing it to interact with and execute Ethereum-based smart contracts seamlessly.
Security and consensus on the Chiliz Chain are maintained through a Proof-of-Staked-Authority (PoSA) mechanism — a hybrid model that combines Proof-of-Authority (PoA) and Proof-of-Stake (PoS). Under PoSA, a limited set of validators take turns producing blocks in a PoA fashion, while their ability to serve as validators depends on the amount of CHZ staked in support of them.
Validators are the backbone of the network, responsible for validating transactions, producing blocks, and safeguarding the chain’s integrity. Two types of validators exist:
*   Main Validators – actively produce blocks and commit them to the blockchain.  
*   Candidate Validators – remain in standby and can be promoted if a Main Validator is penalized or becomes unavailable.
Beyond securing the network, validators also play a crucial role in on-chain governance. Their voting power is proportional to the amount of CHZ staked, giving them influence over proposals that shape the evolution of the chain.
Community members can contribute to network security as delegators, by staking their CHZ with validators. Delegators indirectly participate in governance while helping to secure the chain. In return, they receive a share of the rewards earned by validators — sourced from transaction tips and CHZ block rewards.
This staking-driven model ensures that the Chiliz Chain remains secure, efficient, and community-governed, while supporting the creation and management of digital assets tailored to sports and entertainment.

## About Chiliz
### Chiliz Tokenomics 2.0
Inflationary Model: An initial 8.80% annual base inflation in Year 1, decreasing gradually each year until stabilizing at a 1.88% inflation floor after 14 years.
Perpetual Burning Mechanism: Inspired by Ethereum’s EIP-1559, the majority of transaction fees are permanently burned at the protocol level, offsetting inflation and creating a balancing effect on total supply.
Circulating Supply: Due to the new model, the supply of CHZ is no longer fixed. At the time of drafting, 12th of September 2025, the circulating supply stands at 9,980,635,902 CHZ, but this figure increases daily as new tokens are minted. Projections estimate the supply will gradually rise to ~15 billion CHZ over 14 years (2038) before stabilizing with the inflation floor.
Allocation of Newly Minted CHZ: Each block introduces new CHZ into circulation, distributed as follows:
*   65% – Allocated to the block-producing validator and shared with their delegators (minus validator commission).  
*   10% – Community Vault, Liquidity Providers (LPs), and Shared Security Restaking Rewards.  
*   25% – Ecosystem & Operational (E&O) Distribution.
This dynamic model ensures that validators and delegators are continuously incentivized, while also providing a sustainable funding mechanism for ecosystem development and security.

Chiliz is a digital token developed for DeFi (decentralized finance) applications. It’s a cryptocurrency driven by the Chiliz blockchain network.
The major decentralized app driven by CHZ blockchain is the Socios.com platform – a rapidly developing sports base. The network’s exclusive currency and payment token is Chiliz coin (CHZ). All sports fans and users of the platform can purchase Fan Tokens using the CHZ cryptocurrency.

## **History of Chiliz blockchain**
Chiliz was birthed in 2012 as an extension of an international entertainment and sports organization, Mediarex Group. Moving on to 2018, the company developed a blockchain-based platform called Socios.com.
On October 18, the organization released the Chiliz token, which became available globally on several crypto exchange platforms.
Following the launch was the company’s first partnership with the Italian-based Turin football club, Juventus. As of November 2019, the football club hosted its FTO (Fan Token Offering), making a sale of about 1.3 million tokens. At the time, the maximum supply was about 20 million.
Toward December 2019, the organization released the Socio website and application. About $66 million from Private Placement was invested in driving this development. Soon the app was deployed on the web and several smart devices.
texts.3:
## **What protocol does Chiliz use?**
The consensus system of the CHZ blockchain is Proof of Authority (PoA). This system functions almost similar to the Proof of Stake consensus mechanism. So, it deals with validator nodes for confirming transactions on the network.
texts.4:
## **What protocol does Chiliz use?**
#### **Validators**
The validators on a Proof of Authority consensus system don’t use staking, tokens, or locking for verifying blocks or transactions. Usually, the transaction verification process involves the identification of validators.
Blocks are added to the network after the approval of accounts called validators. These validators focus on putting transactions in blocks using a particular software.
The process is automatic, so validators don’t have to monitor their computers the whole time. However, maintaining these authority nodes (the computers) is very crucial.
As per rewards, the PoA system is similar to PoS. Validators in both systems receive their rewards from the network transaction fees.

## About Chiliz
### How Is the Chiliz Network Secured?
The Chiliz Chain is a dedicated Layer-1 blockchain built for the sports and entertainment industries. It is a fork of BNB Smart Chain (BSC), which itself derives from go-Ethereum (geth). This makes the network Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) compatible, allowing it to interact with and execute Ethereum-based smart contracts seamlessly.
Security and consensus on the Chiliz Chain are maintained through a Proof-of-Staked-Authority (PoSA) mechanism — a hybrid model that combines Proof-of-Authority (PoA) and Proof-of-Stake (PoS). Under PoSA, a limited set of validators take turns producing blocks in a PoA fashion, while their ability to serve as validators depends on the amount of CHZ staked in support of them.
Validators are the backbone of the network, responsible for validating transactions, producing blocks, and safeguarding the chain’s integrity. Two types of validators exist:
*   Main Validators – actively produce blocks and commit them to the blockchain.  
*   Candidate Validators – remain in standby and can be promoted if a Main Validator is penalized or becomes unavailable.
Beyond securing the network, validators also play a crucial role in on-chain governance. Their voting power is proportional to the amount of CHZ staked, giving them influence over proposals that shape the evolution of the chain.
Community members can contribute to network security as delegators, by staking their CHZ with validators. Delegators indirectly participate in governance while helping to secure the chain. In return, they receive a share of the rewards earned by validators — sourced from transaction tips and CHZ block rewards.
This staking-driven model ensures that the Chiliz Chain remains secure, efficient, and community-governed, while supporting the creation and management of digital assets tailored to sports and entertainment.

Inflationary Model: An initial 8.80% annual base inflation in Year 1, decreasing gradually each year until stabilizing at a 1.88% inflation floor after 14 years.
Perpetual Burning Mechanism: Inspired by Ethereum’s EIP-1559, the majority of transaction fees are permanently burned at the protocol level, offsetting inflation and creating a balancing effect on total supply.
Circulating Supply: Due to the new model, the supply of CHZ is no longer fixed. Projections estimate the supply will gradually rise to ~15 billion CHZ over 14 years (2038) before stabilizing with the inflation floor.
Allocation of Newly Minted CHZ: Each block introduces new CHZ into circulation, distributed as follows:
*   65% – Allocated to the block-producing validator and shared with their delegators (minus validator commission).  
*   10% – Community Vault, Liquidity Providers (LPs), and Shared Security Restaking Rewards.  
*   25% – Ecosystem & Operational (E&O) Distribution.
This dynamic model ensures that validators and delegators are continuously incentivized, while also providing a sustainable funding mechanism for ecosystem development and security.

Whether CHZ is a good investment depends on whether fan-token activity can rebuild demand for the token, and the 2026 evidence does not yet show that. CHZ trades at **$0.01216**, and the token is **98.62%** below its all-time high of **$0.8786**. On current data, the case looks speculative rather than fundamentally strong.

## Fundamental strengths and weaknesses
CHZ is the native token of Chiliz Chain, an EVM-compatible layer 1 built for sports and entertainment. It pays network fees, supports governance and is used to buy Fan Tokens on Socios.com. Chiliz reports more than 70 sports organizations issuing Fan Tokens and more than 2 million Fan Token wallets, but these figures are company-reported and independently unverified.
The main weakness is narrow utility. Circulating supply is 10,590,072,875 CHZ against a total supply of 10,590,270,130 CHZ, so there is little supply-side scarcity, and price depends on demand growth. The market cap of **$128.75M** (rank #335) reflects this.

## Adoption and revenue model
DefiLlama shows Chiliz Chain TVL at **$1.44M** as of 1 November 2026, with 7-day DEX volume of **$216,849**. No independent figures for active users or transaction volume were available.
Ten percent of Fan Token transaction and marketplace proceeds funds CHZ buybacks that are burned. Chiliz's Burn Report #7 (26 October 2026) puts cumulative burns at 69,918,100.28 CHZ, roughly **0.66%** of circulating supply. The September burn figure differs between two Chiliz reports, which reduces confidence in the burn data. Issuer filings show Fan Token-related revenue rising from CHF 50.8M in 2024 to CHF 73.3M in 2025, but the filings describe "significant progress toward break-even," which indicates the business is not yet profitable.

## Team credibility and governance
Alexandre Dreyfus serves as founder and CEO of The Chiliz Group and Socios.com. Chief Technology Officer Thibaut Pelletier left in May 2026 after eight years, and no successor was named in the retrieved data. Aggregator data reports headcount declines of 8 to **9%** at Chiliz. The "**$700 million**" revenue claim is self-reported and measures gross sports-industry activity rather than token-level income.

## Regulatory and institutional position
Socios Europe Services received MiCA crypto-asset service provider authorization from Malta's regulator on 11 September 2025. The SEC and CFTC issued joint interpretive guidance on 17 March 2026 that, according to Chiliz, classifies Fan Tokens as digital collectibles and digital tools.
Several risks remain open. A Wealthsimple help page (22 September 2026) states that the SEC has alleged CHZ is a security in pending enforcement proceedings, and the retrieved sources do not include case details or status. Coinbase suspended the CHZ/USDT pair in August 2026 in a low-liquidity review, and GMO Coin is scheduled to delist CHZ on 24 October 2026. The Socios Equity Token, a planned tokenized equity product, is not yet available for purchase.

## Market cycles and derivatives
CHZ traded between **$0.03** and **$0.04** in late June 2026, so the current price is more than **59%** below that range. Derivatives data points to thinning participation. Open interest is **$15.24M**, down **35.68%** over 90 days. Funding is neutral at **0.0011%** per 8 hours, and 24-hour liquidations were negligible. The broader Fear and Greed Index reads 35, classified as Fear.

## Bull and bear cases
**Bull case:** CHZ has a recognized brand and a broad partner network. Buybacks and burns are live, MiCA authorization is in place, and the token has expanded to Solana and Base. Five U.S. universities launched Fan Tokens in July 2026.
**Bear case:** The price trend is weak across all recent timeframes. On-chain TVL is small, adoption data is mostly company-reported, and the SEC allegation is unresolved. Technical leadership has changed, open interest is falling, and the equity product that would broaden the thesis is not yet live.

## Risk/reward assessment
The 2026 record shows execution on several announced milestones, including EU authorization, multi-chain expansion and a functioning burn mechanism. Against that, usage is minimal, burn volumes are small relative to supply, and a security incident on 26 October 2026 led the company to pause its bridge, according to a company statement that says user wallets were unaffected. On current evidence, the downside risk is larger than the identifiable upside, and the outcome depends on a fan-token demand recovery that has not yet appeared in the data.

## **What protocol does Chiliz use?**
#### **Validators**
The validators on a Proof of Authority consensus system don’t use staking, tokens, or locking for verifying blocks or transactions. Usually, the transaction verification process involves the identification of validators.
Blocks are added to the network after the approval of accounts called validators. These validators focus on putting transactions in blocks using a particular software.
The process is automatic, so validators don’t have to monitor their computers the whole time. However, maintaining these authority nodes (the computers) is very crucial.
As per rewards, the PoA system is similar to PoS. Validators in both systems receive their rewards from the network transaction fees.

#### Tokenizing Real World Experiences
**Season 2 Episode 19: Ed Vincent, CEO and Founder of FestivalPass**
Peter is joined by Ed Vincent, CEO and Founder of FestivalPass, to explore a real-time example of how a business can incorporate blockchain and leverage web3 to improve their business model. They discuss Ed's vision behind FestivalPass enhancing the consumer experience for live events, the importance of community building, and how they're using NFTs.

#### Focus Shift to Building & Infrastructure
**Season 2 Episode 18: Jeff Dorman, CIO and Co-founder of Arca**
Jeff Dorman, CIO and Co-founder of Arca, is back again to discuss the current state of the market. Gain a better understanding of what's driving these quieter times as Peter and Jeff discuss regional bank failures, the trickle down effects of meme coins, and the current regulatory environment. Bonus: CA and TX little league baseball and softball updates!

#### The ESG & Value Narratives of Bitcoin Mining
**Season 2 Episode 17: William Szamosszegi, Founder and CEO of Sazminin**
Peter is joined by William Szamosszegi, Founder and CEO of Sazmining, for a robust discussion on bitcoin mining including its effects on the power grid and other mainstream narratives. Learn more about bitcoin as an ESG investment, how it can be used to preserve wealth, and the potential for revolutionizing current financial systems.

#### The Financialization of the NFT Market
**Season 2 Episode 16: Nick Emmons, Co-founder and CEO of Upshot**
Peter is joined by Nick Emmons, Co-founder and CEO of Upshot (upshot.xyz), an NFT appraiser providing insights into NFT markets. Nick and Peter have an interesting discussion around the financialization of NFTs including nuanced problems around custodianship and blockers to further adoption of NFTs in the financial system. Learn about tokenized rewards programs utilized in a crypto native way, tracking grey markets, and the equivalent of a FICO score system for wallets in the NFT ecosystem. Learn more about NFTs from Arca specialists here: https://www.ar.ca/nft

#### New Age Investing: Bitcoin vs. Banks
**Season 2 Episode 15: Jeff Dorman, CIO and Co-founder of Arca**
Jeff Dorman, CIO and Co-founder of Arca, is back with Peter on this week's Between2Chains to provide his insight into the recent market events, what it means for digital assets and the macroeconomy as a whole. Listen to their discussion to learn about tokens as downside protection, a secular shift in thinking, and assigning value to digital and traditional assets.

#### Unique Use-cases for Blockchain Technology
**Season 2 Episode 14: Megan Knab, Co-founder and CEO of Franklin**
This week Peter is joined by Megan Knab, Co-founder and CEO of Franklin, a hybrid crypto and cash payroll software. Gain unique insights into use cases of blockchain technology and trends in the crypto industry as they discuss stablecoin regulation, outdated Tradfi infrastructures, and more.

#### Crypto’s Resiliency in The Wake of Regulation
**Season 2 Episode 13: Jeff Dorman, CIO and Co-founder of Arca**
Jeff Dorman, CIO and Co-founder of Arca, is back to provide an update on markets and give his take on the current crypto rally. Learn how to invest in this uncertain environment, the effects of broad sweeping versus targeted regulatory actions, and the resiliency of digital assets. Bonus: Peter and Jeff get ready to take on another season of youth baseball and softball.

Gain a better understanding of blockchain technology and the investment opportunities it can afford.

#### The Inevitable Convergence of TradFi & Crypto
**Season 2 Episode 11: Featuring Michelle Noyes, Head of Americas at AIMA**
Michelle Noyes, Head of Americas at AIMA and Peter agree on a major theme and that is the inevitable convergence of TradFi and the Crypto industry. Listen to their discussion and learn how legacy institutions reacted to the first crypto winter and how recent market events have impacted their interest in digital assets.

**Season 2 Episode 10: Featuring Rayne Steinberg and Jeff Dorman**

Listen to find out how their knowledge and research coupled with anecdotal conversations they've held with Tradfi professionals and crypto natives have shaped their predictions for market opportunities this year.

#### The Misconception of Crypto as an Asset Class
**Season 2 Episode 9: Featuring Byron Gilliam**
Peter is joined by Byron Gilliam, Markets Strategist and Newsletter Writer at Blockworks, to discuss where we are in the market cycle, core issues and misperceptions in the digital asset industry, and why they are more bullish on crypto as a technology than an investable asset class.

**Season 2 Episode 8: Featuring Alexandre Dreyfus**

Learn how Chiliz is using this revolutionary technology to better align the sports fan to the organization through transparency and fairness.

#### So Now What? The Future of Blockchain
**Season 2 Episode 7: Featuring James Healy**
